title: Sam Bankman-Fried tells teen podcaster that AI has a 25% chance of destroying humanity
excerpt: Sam Bankman-Fried, an early investor in Anthropic, shared his outlook on AI in a prison phone interview with 14-year-old podcaster Eli Goldfine.

Will artificial intelligence destroy humanity?

Sam Bankman-Fried, an early investor in Anthropic now serving a 25-year prison sentence for fraud, shared his guesstimate in a phone interview with a 14-year-old podcaster.

"I would say, like, less than 50%, more than 10%," Bankman-Fried told Eli Goldfine in a call from federal prison in Lompoc, California. "You know, somewhere in the 25% range."

Business Insider earlier this year wrote about the precocious prediction markets guru from Westchester County, New York, who interviews industry players for his Supercycle newsletter and podcast. Bankman-Fried may be his biggest get yet. Eli shared a recording of the interview with Business Insider ahead of its Friday release.

The roughly 90-minute conversation was conducted on Saturday and Sunday over a series of phone calls. Bankman-Fried discussed the downfall of his crypto exchange FTX, his continued belief in the effective altruism movement, and his thoughts on AI. The calls were punctuated by a robotic voice stating that the calls were being recorded and monitored. Bankman-Fried had to repeatedly hang up and call Eli back.

Bankman-Fried was the leading investor in Anthropic's April 2022 Series B round, putting $500 million into the company. The stake was worth about 13.6% of the company at the time.

Bankman-Fried's Anthropic shares ended up in bankruptcy court and were sold in 2024 for a total of $1.3 billion. The money was used to pay FTX's creditors, including victims of the fraud.

After Anthropic's initial public offering Thursday, the AI company's shares were trading at around $97. At that price, Bankman-Fried's shares would have been worth over $40 billion.

"I don't know how much tech news you're getting, but I assume you've probably heard that Anthropic is gonna IPO probably sometime this week," Eli said to Bankman-Fried. "What are your thoughts on their current valuations?"

Bankman-Fried replied that he was still bullish.

In 2023, a jury found Bankman-Fried guilty of fraud and money laundering for an $11 billion scheme in which he commingled funds belonging to customers of FTX, his cryptocurrency exchange, with Alameda Research, his crypto hedge fund. In September of this year, he asked the US Supreme Court to consider his appeal.

In his interview, Eli asked Bankman-Fried to predict the "P(doom)," a term that a very-online mix of AI enthusiasts and opponents use to refer to the probability of an AI-driven catastrophe that wipes out the human race.

Bankman-Fried said one of the reasons it's hard to settle on a single figure is because different people may have different ideas about what makes a "catastrophic event."

"What if you have a world where humans start uploading their brains and non-upload humans get sort of passed by — is that a catastrophic event? Different people give different answers to that question," he said. "So depending on that, I think I could answer anywhere between, like, 20 and 60 percent, depending on those sort of gray areas."

According to Bankman-Fried, the probability rests, in part, on whether humans and artificial intelligence have a "peaceful coexistence" or whether "AI will just get bored of humanity and wipe it out."

"Some chance of synergistic work, driven largely by AI, but with human goals in mind — that will lead to massive, massive technological expansion," he said.

Eli asked if Bankman-Fried would consider uploading his own brain into the wide expanse of the internet.

"Potentially," said the 34-year-old former tech billionaire who's scheduled to be stuck in prison until 2043. "Obviously, devil's in the details, but I don't have any per se objection to it."
